metadata.subtitle: Fugue XVIII in G-sharp minor, five voices: Vigilate
metadata.composer: Claude / Sam (door subject after J. S. Bach, BWV 61 no. 4)
metadata.tempo_text: Vigilate: from the evening to the morning

markers.label: II. Media nocte (midnight): the knock; Aeolian, A#
Summit: three entries a third apart

subject_entries.label: I. Sero (evening): subject, Phrygian (A natural)
I: answer on D#
I: subject
I: answer on D#, in the bass
II. Media nocte (midnight): door subject (BWV 61), the fifth voice enters
II: subject, Aeolian (A#), over the door subject in thirds
II: door subject on A#, to a half close on D#
II: door subject in the soprano, above the subject in the bass
II: subject in the bass, under the door subject (parts exchanged)
II: door subject on F#, landing on a downbeat: cadence in B major
III. Galli cantu (cockcrow): door subject in the bass
III: subject, Dorian (E#): the leap B-E# is the cockcrow
III: door subject above the tenor (parts exchanged)
III: subject in the tenor: the cock crows again (b31.1)
III: stretto, the subject two beats later a tenth higher (on B, inside the same scale)
III: door subject on C#, landing on a downbeat: cadence in F-sharp major
IV. Mane (morning): door subject in the tenor
IV: subject, Mixolydian (B#): G-sharp major at b36.3
IV: summit, the subject a third higher every two beats (on G#)
IV: summit, the subject a third higher every two beats (on B#)

The last knock: door subject in the fifth voice, an octave above its first knock
Dawn: subject, Ionian, in A-flat major, straight out of the door subject
Dawn: stretto, the subject a sixth lower, two beats later
Dawn: answer in the bass
Dawn: the subject in the soprano; its G rises to A-flat (b52.1)
